content: 1. Tecovirimat may reduce the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of certain drugs, such as toremifene, trabectedin, tramadol, trazodone, triazolam, trimethoprim, ulipristal, valbenazine, vandetanib, vardenafil, venetoclax, venlafaxine, verapamil, vilazodone, vinblastine, vincristine, vincristine liposomal, vinorelbine, vorapaxar, vortioxetine, and zonisamide. This occurs due to its weak induction of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is involved in drug metabolism. Close monitoring of these drugs is recommended when co-administered with tecovirimat to ensure therapeutic effectiveness. 2. Tecovirimat is a weak inducer of CYP3A4. When co-administered with drugs metabolized by this enzyme, such as those listed above, their effectiveness may be reduced. It is essential to monitor the plasma levels and clinical response of these drugs closely. 3. Tecovirimat may increase the plasma concentration or therapeutic effect of certain drugs, such as treprostinil, tretinoin, trimipramine, velpatasvir, voriconazole, and voxilaprevir. This is due to its weak inhibition of the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Close monitoring is advised to avoid potential adverse effects. 4. Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. When co-administered with drugs metabolized by these enzymes, such as those listed above, there is a potential for increased drug levels and associated adverse effects. Monitoring for toxicity is recommended. 5. Co-administration of tecovirimat with ublixtuximab may reduce the effectiveness of tecovirimat due to the immunosuppressive effects of ublixtuximab, which may increase the risk of infection. Close monitoring is advised. 6. Co-administration of tecovirimat with repaglinide, an antidiabetic agent, may result in mild-to-moderate hypoglycemia. Blood glucose levels should be monitored, and patients should be observed for symptoms of hypoglycemia. 7. There is no available data on the use of tecovirimat in pregnant women. The potential benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child or from the underlying maternal condition. 8. Tecovirimat capsules should be taken within 30 minutes after consuming a full meal containing moderate or high fat to ensure optimal absorption. 9. Tecovirimat capsules should be stored in their original bottle at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with excursions permitted to 15–30°C (59–86°F). Unopened vials should be refrigerated at 2–8°C (36–46°F) and should not be frozen. 10. For tecovirimat injection, the solution should be prepared using 0.9% NaCl or D5W in a syringe of suitable size. Other diluents have not been studied. The solution should be infused over 6 hours every 12 hours for 14 days. It is not intended for IV bolus injection. Prefilled infusion bags should not be used for preparation or administration. The solution should be gently swirled before use, and single-dose vials should be discarded after puncture. 11.
